hero.headline: Twelve people shot near street festival in Toledo, Ohio
hero.body:
Police in Toledo, Ohio are searching for suspects after twelve people were shot near a street festival. Authorities say it appears two people fired weapons and were likely shooting at each other.

The victims range in age from 14 to 61 years old. Police have not announced any arrests and continue to search for the suspects involved in the shooting.

The shooting occurred near a street festival in the Toledo area. Authorities responded to reports of gunfire and found multiple victims at the scene. The incident led to a large police presence in the area as investigators worked to determine what happened.

Police believe the shooting was not random and that the two shooters were targeting each other. Bystanders and festival attendees appear to have been caught in the crossfire. Law enforcement has not released information about the condition of the victims or whether any have life-threatening injuries.

Authorities are asking anyone with information about the shooting to contact Toledo police. The investigation remains active as police work to identify and locate the suspects.

cards.headline: US forces shoot down Iranian drones in Strait of Hormuz as military standoff continues
cards.body:
The US military shot down two Iranian drones in the Strait of Hormuz following an exchange of strikes between the two countries, marking another escalation in their ongoing conflict. The incident occurred as the Trump administration intensifies pressure on Iran to reach a negotiated settlement.

According to US military statements, Iran launched missiles and drones toward the strategic waterway, prompting the American response. Iran subsequently accused the United States of violating a ceasefire agreement, claiming that Tehran had targeted US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. The tense exchange underscores the fragile situation in the region despite ongoing diplomatic efforts.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world's most critical shipping lanes, with significant portions of global oil traffic passing through its narrow waters. The US military characterized the Iranian drones as posing a threat to commercial shipping in the area. Both countries maintain strong interests in the region, and the waterway has repeatedly become a flashpoint for military confrontations between Washington and Tehran.

Peace negotiations between the two nations have stalled, with neither side making substantial progress toward resolving their broader conflict. The latest strikes demonstrate how quickly tensions can escalate even as diplomatic channels theoretically remain open.

The Trump administration is also considering a financial response to the crisis. According to sources, the Treasury Department is planning to make frozen Iranian assets available to US Gulf allies as compensation for damage sustained during recent hostilities. This proposal would redirect seized Iranian funds toward reconstruction efforts in allied nations bordering the strategic waterway, including Kuwait and Bahrain.

The United States maintains a substantial naval presence in the Persian Gulf to protect international shipping lanes and support allied countries in the region. Iran has conducted multiple military exercises and deployed forces near the strait during previous periods of heightened tension, using such actions to assert its regional interests.

The military situation reflects broader concerns about stability in the Middle East. Both nations appear willing to engage in direct military action while simultaneously pursuing diplomatic solutions, creating an unpredictable security environment for regional commerce and international shipping.

The incident involving the drones and missiles represents the latest in a series of exchanges between the two countries. Defense officials have characterized the current situation as fragile, with the potential for broader conflict if either side miscalculates or if diplomatic negotiations fail to produce concrete results.

The combination of military pressure and financial incentives suggests the Trump administration is pursuing a multifaceted strategy aimed at compelling Iran to negotiate. Whether these efforts will succeed in breaking the diplomatic stalemate remains uncertain as both sides continue their military posturing in one of the world's most strategically important waterways.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches hundreds of drones targeting Russian military sites after Putin rejects talks
cards.teaser: Ukraine conducted mass drone strikes on Russian military facilities including a naval base near St. Petersburg after President Putin declined a meeting with President Zelenskyy.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched hundreds of drones targeting Russian military facilities, including strikes on a navy base near St. Petersburg, following President Vladimir Putin's rejection of a proposed direct meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The long-range attacks hit multiple sites across Russia on the final day of Putin's appearance at an international summit in Davos.

The drone strikes represented one of the largest coordinated aerial attacks Ukraine has conducted against Russian military infrastructure. The targeting of facilities near St. Petersburg marked a significant escalation in Ukraine's willingness to strike deep inside Russian territory. Putin had declined Zelenskyy's offer for direct negotiations, prompting Ukraine to continue its military campaign against Russian strategic assets.

The victims range in age from 14 to 61 years old. Police have not announced any arrests and continue to search for the suspects involved in the shooting.

Law enforcement has not released information about the condition of the victims or whether any have life-threatening injuries.

Authorities are asking anyone with information about the shooting to contact Toledo police. The investigation remains active as police work to identify and locate the suspects.

cards.headline: Federal probe launched into California election process
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorney's office in California has announced an investigation into the state's elections as millions of ballots remain uncounted.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles to observe ballot processing in California's governor's race, as the state continues counting millions of outstanding ballots from the primary election.

The delayed results have sparked claims of election fraud and rigging from national figures, though state officials have rejected these allegations. Experts warn that ballot-counting could extend through the governor's race as well as concurrent primary elections for LA mayor and Congress.

cards.headline: States prepare lawsuit to block Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery
cards.teaser: Multiple US states are preparing legal action to stop Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, according to sources.
cards.body:
US state attorneys general are preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. The $110 billion deal has drawn opposition from industry workers and legal challenges. Sources confirmed that multiple states are coordinating legal action against the merger.

A town hall meeting for industry workers opposed to the deal featured emotional testimony. Paramount has offered to sell its kids channels to address European Union regulatory concerns. A Paramount lawyer claimed some opponents of the Warner Bros deal hold antisemitic views, according to reports.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced Saturday that it has launched an investigation into election fraud in California's elections. The probe comes as vote counting continues in several key races across the state.

The announcement follows unsubstantiated claims by President Trump and other conservatives about irregularities in California's vote-counting process. Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy also criticized the state's vote-counting procedures, saying California voters were losing faith in the process as results continue to come in from Tuesday's primary elections.

cards.headline: Armenia votes as Russia pressures government seeking closer ties with West
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeks a third term in parliamentary elections as Russia applies pressure on his government over its pivot toward Western partnerships.
cards.body:
Armenia held parliamentary elections with incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeking a third term despite falling domestic support. Russia has increased pressure on Pashinyan's government over its shift toward closer relations with Western countries.

Pashinyan has faced declining popularity at home while navigating tensions with Russia, Armenia's traditional security partner. His government has pursued warmer ties with Western nations, drawing scrutiny from Moscow. The election results will determine whether Armenian voters support continuing this strategic reorientation or prefer a return to closer alignment with Russia.

cards.headline: Neo-Nazi party candidate advances to mayoral runoff in German town
cards.teaser: A member of a neo-Nazi party reached the final round of a mayoral election in a small eastern German town, potentially breaking a post-World War II pattern of voters rejecting such candidates.
cards.body:
A candidate from a neo-Nazi party qualified for the runoff election in a mayoral race in a small town in eastern Germany. Since the fall of the Third Reich, German voters have consistently rejected mayoral candidates from neo-Nazi parties in final elections.

The runoff election was scheduled for Sunday. The advancement of a neo-Nazi candidate to the final round represents a potential shift in local German politics, particularly in eastern regions. German voters have historically used their ballots to block extremist candidates from winning local offices, making this development significant for observers of German democracy.

cards.headline: US defense secretary delivers D-Day speech criticizing European migration policy
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a Normandy ceremony marking 82 years since the Allied invasion to attack European governments over migration, describing arrivals as a beach invasion.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered a speech in Normandy on the 82nd anniversary of D-Day, using the occasion to criticize European migration policy. He characterized migrant arrivals using military language, drawing an unconventional parallel between current migration and the Allied beach landing.

The remarks marked a significant departure from traditional D-Day commemorations, which typically honor the soldiers who fought in the 1944 invasion to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. Hegseth's speech took place at official ceremonies attended by government representatives and veterans.

cards.headline: Senegal president and prime minister locked in power struggle threatening government stability
cards.teaser: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and former Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko are fighting for control after the two allies defeated Senegal's political establishment together.
cards.body:
Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and former Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko, who together defeated the country's political establishment, are now locked in conflict. After Sonko's removal as prime minister, he withdrew his political party from the government and was re-elected to lead it, signaling his continued political ambitions.

The rift jeopardizes Senegal's stability and its international commitments. Sonko has threatened to boycott as Faye formed a new cabinet, creating uncertainty about the government's direction and an IMF agreement the country depends on.

cards.headline: Former child soldier in Somalia recounts forced combat and lasting trauma
cards.teaser: Yusuf Ali, now 34, describes being forced to kill as a child soldier in Somalia and continues to struggle with memories while living in Mogadishu.
cards.body:
Yusuf Ali, now 34, was forced into combat as a child soldier in Somalia. He describes the experience as one of survival, where the choice was between killing or being killed. Today, living in Mogadishu, Ali remains haunted by his past.

Years after his time as a child combatant, Ali continues to struggle with nightmares and difficult memories. Surrounded by reminders of his traumatic experiences in his hometown, he carries the lasting psychological scars of his forced involvement in armed conflict.

cards.headline: Federal probe launched into California election process
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorney's office in California has announced an investigation into the state's elections as millions of ballots remain uncounted.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles to observe ballot processing in California's governor's race, as the state continues counting millions of outstanding ballots from the primary election.

The delayed results have sparked claims of election fraud and rigging from national figures, though state officials have rejected these allegations. Experts warn that ballot-counting could extend through the governor's race as well as concurrent primary elections for LA mayor and Congress.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump has pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading.
cards.body:
President Trump pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who served nearly two years in prison for insider trading. Buyer was sentenced to 22 months in 2023 after making illegal stock trades based on confidential information obtained while working as a consultant and lobbyist following his time in Congress. He was released in 2025.

As part of his sentence, Buyer was ordered to forfeit over $350,000 in illegal gains and pay a $10,000 fine. The pardon comes as Trump's administration has promoted efforts to crack down on fraud in Democratic-led states.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as vote count continues
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman has closed the gap with Spencer Pratt as additional votes are tallied in the Los Angeles mayoral primary.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt's lead over Nithya Raman has narrowed as more votes in the Los Angeles mayoral race are counted. The race remains competitive with millions of California ballots still being processed statewide.

Voters are awaiting results in both the Los Angeles mayoral race and the California governor's race. The candidates include former Mayor Karen Bass, Nithya Raman, and Spencer Pratt, with results showing different geographic strengths for each candidate across the city.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers authorize strike ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Workers at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles have voted to authorize a strike as the venue prepares to host World Cup matches.
cards.body:
Workers at SoFi Stadium have voted to authorize a strike as the Los Angeles venue prepares to host World Cup games. The authorization gives the union leverage in ongoing contract negotiations.

Union representatives, the stadium's hospitality group, and FIFA are continuing talks, with negotiations scheduled to resume Monday.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes Europe on migration in D-Day speech
cards.teaser: U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth spoke about European migration policy during a speech in Normandy marking the 82nd anniversary of D-Day.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Hegseth attacked Europe over migration during a speech in Normandy, 82 years after the D-Day landings. He used language describing a beach invasion while speaking at the site where allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe.

His comments on migration represented a departure from traditional D-Day commemorative remarks, which typically focus on the historical military operation and the alliance between the United States and European nations.

cards.headline: UK defense plan delays criticized by lawmakers
cards.teaser: British lawmakers say delays to the Defence Investment Plan undermine the country's credibility ahead of a NATO summit.
cards.body:
Members of Parliament criticized delays to the UK's Defence Investment Plan, saying the postponements harm British credibility. The plan is now scheduled for release before a NATO summit early next month.

The delays have raised concerns among lawmakers about the government's commitment to defense spending. The timing is significant as NATO allies prepare to meet and discuss collective security arrangements.

hero.headline: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 in worst weekly drop since FTX collapse
hero.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 this week, marking the lowest level since October 2024. The cryptocurrency suffered its worst weekly decline since the November 2022 collapse of the FTX exchange. Ether and other major cryptocurrencies also posted steep losses during the same period.

The sell-off erased all gains Bitcoin had accumulated since the November 2024 presidential election. The price decline represents a significant reversal for cryptocurrency markets, which had rallied following the election results. Multiple cryptocurrencies experienced double-digit percentage losses over the week.

The current downturn has brought Bitcoin back near its 2026 low. Trading activity reflected widespread selling pressure across cryptocurrency exchanges. The sharp decline prompted comparisons to previous major market corrections in the digital asset sector.

Market analysts have noted the severity of the weekly losses. The FTX collapse in late 2022 triggered a prolonged downturn in cryptocurrency prices and shook confidence in digital asset platforms. The current decline matches that period in terms of weekly percentage losses.

The broader cryptocurrency market followed Bitcoin lower. Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, also posted significant losses. The synchronized decline across major digital assets indicates widespread investor concern rather than issues specific to individual cryptocurrencies.

cards.headline: SpaceX faces skepticism over proposed $1.8 trillion valuation for public offering
cards.teaser: Wall Street analysts question whether SpaceX's planned initial public offering can succeed at its proposed $1.8 trillion valuation.
cards.body:
SpaceX is considering an initial public offering that would value the company at $1.8 trillion. Wall Street observers have expressed doubt about whether the market can absorb a public offering of that size. The valuation would make it one of the largest IPOs in history.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon hosted an event focused on the SpaceX offering. The company's proposed valuation has drawn comparisons to previous large-scale public offerings. Analysts have described the offering as a test of market capacity for extremely high-value technology stocks.

cards.headline: States prepare lawsuit to block Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery
cards.teaser: Multiple US states are preparing legal action to stop Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, according to sources.
cards.body:
US state attorneys general are preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. The $110 billion deal has drawn opposition from industry workers and legal challenges. Sources confirmed that multiple states are coordinating legal action against the merger.

A town hall meeting for industry workers opposed to the deal featured emotional testimony. Paramount has offered to sell its kids channels to address European Union regulatory concerns. A Paramount lawyer claimed some opponents of the Warner Bros deal hold antisemitic views, according to reports.

cards.headline: Broadcom stock drops on weak software revenue and unchanged AI chip forecast
cards.teaser: Broadcom shares declined after the company reported weak software sales and maintained its existing forecast for AI chip revenue.
cards.body:
Broadcom stock fell following earnings results that showed weaker than expected software sales. The company also left its AI chip revenue forecast for the year unchanged. Multiple analysts adjusted their price targets for the stock following the earnings report.

Bank of America reset its Broadcom price target after reviewing the earnings results. Some analysts described the stock decline as an overreaction to what they characterized as conservative guidance from management. The company's valuation has been analyzed as premium relative to other semiconductor manufacturers.

cards.headline: Pfizer obesity drug shows similar side effects to Wegovy in midstage trial
cards.teaser: Pfizer's monthly obesity injection produced a side effect profile comparable to existing treatments in a midstage clinical trial.
cards.body:
Pfizer reported results from a midstage trial of its monthly obesity injection. The drug showed a side effect profile similar to Wegovy, an existing weight loss medication. The pharmaceutical company is positioning weight loss drugs as a key part of its growth strategy for the next decade.

The trial data arrives as drugmakers compete to develop obesity treatments that require fewer injections. Pfizer's candidate is being tested as a once-monthly shot. Analysts have suggested that competition in the crowded obesity drug market may increasingly focus on pricing and dosing frequency.

cards.headline: Major corporations fund training programs to address shortage of mechanics and electricians
cards.teaser: Large US companies are investing in training programs to develop skilled tradespeople as the country faces shortages of mechanics and electricians.
cards.body:
The U.S. faces a significant shortage of skilled trades workers, prompting major corporations to invest in training programs. Ford's CEO has warned that the lack of blue-collar workers could drive up consumer costs. A collision repair industry report found that technician training programs currently fill only 42 percent of the demand for qualified workers.

Private companies are funding vocational training initiatives to develop the next generation of mechanics and electricians. These efforts aim to close the skills gap across multiple industries by creating new pathways into technical careers.

cards.headline: WWE shareholder lawsuit trial canceled and removed from court calendar
cards.teaser: A trial for a WWE shareholder lawsuit related to the company's merger has been canceled and taken off the court schedule.
cards.body:
The trial for a WWE shareholder lawsuit has been officially canceled. The case had been scheduled to go to trial and involved litigation over WWE's merger. The removal from the court calendar spares WWE executives, including Vince McMahon, from testifying at this time.

Multiple wrestling industry publications reported that the trial was removed from the court schedule. The shareholder lawsuit had been set to examine details of the WWE merger transaction. No new trial date has been announced following the cancellation.

hero.headline: OpenAI introduces Lockdown Mode to defend against prompt injection attacks
hero.body:
OpenAI released a new security feature called Lockdown Mode designed to protect sensitive data from prompt injection attacks. The feature aims to reduce the likelihood that ChatGPT will share confidential information when attackers attempt to manipulate the system through carefully crafted prompts.

Prompt injection attacks exploit how AI systems process instructions by inserting malicious commands that can cause the model to behave in unintended ways. These attacks pose particular risks when ChatGPT processes sensitive business data or personal information. An attacker might embed hidden instructions in documents or messages that trick the AI into revealing confidential details it should keep private.

Lockdown Mode represents OpenAI's response to this growing security concern as more organizations integrate ChatGPT into workflows that handle proprietary or personal data. The company acknowledged that even with the new protection, ChatGPT remains potentially vulnerable to prompt injections. The goal is not to eliminate the risk entirely but to make it significantly harder for attackers to successfully extract sensitive information through these techniques.

The security enhancement comes as AI systems face increasing scrutiny over data protection and privacy. Companies deploying ChatGPT for customer service, document processing, and internal communications need assurance that the system will not inadvertently leak confidential information. Prompt injection has emerged as one of the more concerning attack vectors because it exploits the fundamental way large language models interpret and follow instructions.

OpenAI did not specify the exact mechanisms Lockdown Mode uses to detect and block prompt injection attempts. The feature adds another layer to the company's security infrastructure as it continues to expand ChatGPT's enterprise and business applications where data protection requirements are strictest.

cards.headline: Apple prepares Siri overhaul and Apple Intelligence updates for WWDC
cards.teaser: Apple's annual developer conference approaches with expected announcements of major improvements to Siri and updates to its Apple Intelligence features.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing to unveil significant changes to Siri alongside updates to its Apple Intelligence platform at the upcoming Worldwide Developers Conference. The event will showcase the company's latest software developments for developers and consumers.

The Siri revamp represents one of the most anticipated announcements at WWDC 2026. Apple Intelligence, the company's suite of AI-powered features, will also receive updates as Apple continues to compete in the artificial intelligence space.

cards.headline: Fossil evidence reveals three-foot scorpion with six-inch pincers
cards.teaser: Scientists identified the largest scorpion ever to exist based on 415-million-year-old fossils showing a creature the size of a baseball bat.
cards.body:
Researchers analyzing fossils from the Devonian Period discovered the largest scorpion species ever documented, measuring over three feet in length with pincers reaching six inches. The ancient creature lived approximately 415 million years ago during a time when scorpions grew to sizes unimaginable today.

The Natural History Museum and other institutions participated in the study of these fossils, which provided new insights into the giant arthropods that once inhabited ancient Britain. The scorpion's size rivaled that of a full-grown German Shepherd, making it one of the most formidable predators of its era.

cards.headline: Scientists removed from diabetes conference after distributing journal reprints
cards.teaser: Conference organizers ejected multiple researchers, including a journal editor-in-chief and former association president, for distributing academic reprints.
cards.body:
The American Diabetes Association ejected several prominent scientists from its conference for distributing reprints of published journal articles. Among those removed were Steven Kahn, editor-in-chief of an ADA journal, and Desmond Schatz, a former ADA president.

The removals sparked concerns about academic freedom and conference policies governing research distribution. The specific reason for the ejections and any further consequences for the scientists remain undisclosed by the ADA.

cards.headline: Stellar Blade sequel Blood Rain announced with AI-generated imagery controversy
cards.teaser: The developers of Stellar Blade revealed a sequel at Summer Game Fest, but the announcement trailer drew criticism for allegedly using AI-generated content.
cards.body:
Stellar Blade: Blood Rain was unveiled at Summer Game Fest with a trailer showcasing stylish combat and expansive cityscapes. The sequel continues the original game's action-focused gameplay while expanding the scale and scope of its environments.

The announcement generated controversy when observers identified what they believed to be generative AI elements in the reveal materials. The developers stated they want to reach as many fans as possible and have not decided on day one platforms, leaving open the possibility of releases on Xbox Series, PC, and PS5.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors studio expands with Japan office and new DLC
cards.teaser: Developer poncle announced a Nintendo Switch 2 version, a Japan studio led by El Shaddai creator Sawaki Takeyasu, and the Legacy of the Blood Moon expansion.
cards.body:
Poncle revealed plans to establish a studio in Japan headed by Sawaki Takeyasu, the creator of El Shaddai. The expansion represents a significant growth move for the Vampire Survivors developer as it builds out its international presence.

The company also announced Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Blood Moon DLC and confirmed the game will launch on Nintendo Switch 2. The announcements signal the studio's commitment to supporting the franchise across multiple platforms while expanding its development capabilities.

cards.headline: Ancient dragonflies reached two-foot wingspans in oxygen-rich atmosphere
cards.teaser: The largest insects ever to live were dragonflies with wingspans exceeding two feet, grown in an ancient atmosphere far richer in oxygen than today.
cards.body:
Scientists studying prehistoric insects found that the largest flying insects in Earth's history were dragonflies with wingspans surpassing two feet. These enormous creatures thrived in an ancient atmosphere that contained significantly higher oxygen concentrations than the air today.

The oxygen-rich environment of the distant past enabled insects to grow to sizes impossible under current atmospheric conditions. Modern insects are constrained by the lower oxygen levels in contemporary air, which cannot support the respiratory needs of such large arthropods.

hero.headline: Marner scores Stanley Cup Final hat trick as Golden Knights edge Hurricanes in double overtime
hero.body:
Mitch Marner scored three goals in the second period of Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, making NHL history as he helped the Vegas Golden Knights defeat the Carolina Hurricanes in double overtime. The Golden Knights now lead the series 2-1 after the dramatic finish in Las Vegas.

Marner's second-period hat trick marked a historic achievement in Stanley Cup Final play, giving Vegas momentum in a game that required two overtime periods to decide. The Hurricanes mounted a comeback attempt after falling behind, forcing the extra frames before ultimately falling short.

The double overtime thriller capped a game built on unusual turns and momentum swings. Carolina fought back from Marner's three-goal outburst to tie the game and send it to overtime, but Vegas ultimately prevailed in the second extra period. The Hurricanes now face a series deficit heading into Game 4.

The Golden Knights have taken control of the series with their home ice advantage, while Carolina must regroup after watching a potential comeback slip away in the second overtime period. The loss leaves the Hurricanes in a difficult position as the series continues.

Game 4 will determine whether Vegas can extend its series lead or if Carolina can even the matchup. The Hurricanes showed resilience in forcing overtime but could not complete the comeback in what became one of the most dramatic games in this year's Final.

cards.headline: Korda shares US Women's Open lead as Hull shoots 65
cards.teaser: Nelly Korda carded a four-under 67 to move into a share of the lead after the third round, while Charley Hull of England shot a 65 to storm into contention.
cards.body:
Nelly Korda moved into a share of the lead at the US Women's Open after carding a four-under par 67 in the third round. The American positioned herself at the top of the leaderboard heading into the final day of competition.

England's Charley Hull made significant ground with an impressive third-round performance, posting a 65 to surge into contention for the title.

cards.headline: Golden Tempo wins Belmont Stakes after Kentucky Derby victory
cards.teaser: Golden Tempo won the Belmont Stakes at Saratoga Race Course, adding to its Kentucky Derby victory from a month earlier.
cards.body:
Golden Tempo won the 158th Belmont Stakes on Saturday at Saratoga Race Course, securing the third leg of the Triple Crown just five weeks after winning the Kentucky Derby. With jockey Jose Ortiz in the saddle, Golden Tempo charged down the stretch to victory at 6-1 odds, holding off second-place finisher Commandment at the wire.

The win marks another historic achievement for trainer Cherie DeVaux, who continues to make history with the horse. Favorite Renegade finished third in the race.

cards.headline: Brazil defeats USWNT 2-1 in international friendly
cards.teaser: Brazil beat the United States women's national team 2-1 in a friendly match in Sao Paulo, spoiling Sophia Wilson's return to the lineup.
cards.body:
Brazil defeated the United States 2-1 in an international friendly on Saturday in Sao Paulo. Sophia Wilson scored in her first appearance for the USWNT since 2024, but Brazil responded with two goals in quick succession to secure the victory.

The match served as World Cup preparation for both nations, with the US beginning their cycle for the 2027 tournament. Despite an early American attack, the hosts' swift counterattack in the second half proved decisive in the friendly clash.

cards.headline: Bonfim defeats Muhammad at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Gabriel Bonfim dominated Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas, winning the main event and calling out Jack Della Maddalena afterward.
cards.body:
Gabriel Bonfim scored a dominant victory over Belal Muhammad in the main event of UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas. The Brazilian fighter controlled the bout from start to finish at UFC Vegas 118.

After the win, Bonfim called out Jack Della Maddalena as a potential next opponent. The victory marked a significant performance for Bonfim in the welterweight division as he looks to climb the rankings.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers authorize strike ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Workers at SoFi Stadium voted to authorize a strike one week before the venue hosts the US men's national team World Cup opener.
cards.body:
Workers at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles voted to authorize a strike ahead of the FIFA World Cup, which begins at the venue in one week. The union vote gives leadership the power to call a walkout if needed, though it does not guarantee one will occur. The timing creates pressure on stadium management as the venue prepares to host the United States men's national team opener.

Negotiations between the union representing stadium workers, the hospitality group at SoFi Stadium, and FIFA are scheduled to continue Monday.

cards.headline: Chase Elliott to lead NASCAR field at Michigan
cards.teaser: Chase Elliott won the pole position for the NASCAR race at Michigan International Speedway, leading Hendrick Motorsports to the front of the starting grid.
cards.body:
Chase Elliott captured the pole position in qualifying at Michigan International Speedway, earning the top starting spot for the NASCAR race. Elliott will lead the Hendrick Motorsports contingent to the green flag.

The qualifying results set the starting order for the weekend race at Michigan. Elliott's performance in qualifying gave him track position advantage heading into the event at the two-mile speedway.

hero.headline: Anthony Head, Actor in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, Dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head played Giles, the school librarian and mentor to Sarah Michelle Gellar's Buffy Summers, throughout the show's seven seasons from 1997 to 2003. The character became a fan favorite for his guidance and dry British wit, helping define the supernatural drama's mix of horror and heart that made it a cultural touchstone of the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Beyond Buffy, Head's career spanned decades across television and film. He appeared in the BBC sketch show Little Britain, the BBC production of Merlin, and films including The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie. More recently, he played Rupert Mannion, a former football club owner, in the acclaimed Apple TV+ series Ted Lasso, where he regularly appeared alongside co-creator Jason Sudeikis and earned praise for their on-screen chemistry.

Head's early career included stage work, beginning with the 1978 West End revival of Godspell. In the 1980s and 1990s, he performed in various theatrical productions including Chess and The Rocky Horror Show. He also sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and appeared on their 1986 debut album.

Before his rise to international fame, Head was well-known in the UK and US for appearing in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements, which featured a slow-burn courtship between a British couple.

Born in Camden, London, Head came from an artistic family. His father was a documentary filmmaker who founded Verity Films, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother was also an actor.

During Buffy's production, Head commuted between Los Angeles and England, where his partner Sarah and two young daughters lived. "I'd try to go home to them every three or four weeks," he told the Guardian in 2016. "Every time I got the chance to have six days clear, I'd get on a plane."

Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute to Head on Instagram, beginning with a quote from her Buffy character: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok." She continued, "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

His daughters noted that his legacy will live on through the shows he appeared in and the audiences who loved them.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo and Robert Smith Debut Duet at Primavera Sound
cards.teaser: The pop star premiered a collaborative song with The Cure's frontman during a surprise festival appearance.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo brought Robert Smith of The Cure on stage at Primavera Sound festival to debut their duet titled What's Wrong With Me. The collaboration appears on Rodrigo's forthcoming album, which releases within the next week.

The surprise performance revealed one of the album's closely guarded secrets. Rodrigo performed a set at the festival that included the premiere of the new track featuring Smith's vocals. The collaboration marks an unexpected pairing between the pop star and the veteran rock musician.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Wed in Sicily Ceremony
cards.teaser: The singer married the actor in Italy with Elton John performing at the celebration.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and actor Callum Turner married in Sicily. Elton John performed his song Your Song during the wedding celebration, according to reports from the event.

The ceremony took place in Italy and drew attention in Palermo. Vanity Fair reported on the wedding, which featured vintage-inspired fashion elements. The couple's wedding included references to how they first met, according to coverage of the event.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Opens Music Center in New Jersey
cards.teaser: The musician's new center for American music opened with performances including Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy.
cards.body:
Bruce Springsteen opened the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music at Monmouth University. The center launched with concerts featuring Springsteen alongside Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy in performances billed as Music America.

The opening took place at the newly established venue in New Jersey. Springsteen performed at the Oakland Arena for fans attending the launch events. The center is dedicated to American music and opened its doors to the public on June 13.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Thanks Supporters After 60 Minutes Departure
cards.teaser: The former correspondent posted on social media following his firing from the news program.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley was fired by CBS News on Tuesday following a clash with the network's new management. In a statement shared on social media Wednesday, the veteran correspondent accused the network's executives of instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting and of silencing employees.

Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes built its decades-long reputation as America's top program through integrity and quality journalism. His firing has sparked concern among viewers and industry observers about the direction of the long-running newsmagazine under its new leadership.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Launches Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland
cards.teaser: The singer performed her first concert tour in more than six years.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande began her Eternal Sunshine tour at Oakland Arena. The concert marked her return to touring after a six and a half year break from the road.

Variety attended the opening night performance and documented the full setlist. The tour takes its name from Grande's album and represents her first extended series of concerts since 2019.

cards.headline: Ye Performs in Netherlands Despite Protests
cards.teaser: The rapper held concerts in Europe after a Dutch court allowed the shows to proceed.
cards.body:
Ye performed for thousands of fans in the Netherlands after a court blocked attempts to stop the concerts. A Jewish group had sought to prevent the shows due to the rapper's previous antisemitic statements.

A Dutch judge ruled that the concerts could proceed despite the protests. Thousands attended the European performances. The Times of Israel and other outlets covered the legal dispute and subsequent shows.

hero.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
hero.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
hero.body:
Deb Haaland, a former official in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. If she prevails in the general election this November, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

Haaland's primary victory sets up a competitive general election race that will determine who succeeds the current governor. Her background and the potential historic significance of her candidacy have drawn national attention to the New Mexico gubernatorial contest.

The race reflects broader patterns emerging across multiple states in this election cycle. Democratic primaries nationwide have highlighted contests with significant historical implications and diverse candidates competing for high-profile positions.

In neighboring states and across the country, Democratic voters have been actively engaged in primary races to determine nominees for major offices. Turnout in several Democratic primaries has been notably high, indicating strong voter participation in nomination contests.

The focus on Haaland's candidacy underscores how gubernatorial races in key states are attracting scrutiny and resources from national political figures and organizations. Her former role in the Biden administration has given her a national profile as she pursues elected office.

The New Mexico Democratic primary victory represents a significant milestone for Haaland personally and carries broader implications for representation in American politics. Her potential to become the first female Native American governor reflects changing demographics and political engagement among historically underrepresented communities.

The general election in November will test whether Haaland's primary success translates into broader appeal across the general electorate. Governors' races have become increasingly competitive in recent years, with both parties investing substantially in key states.

Haaland's campaign message and policy positions resonated with primary voters in New Mexico. Her background and experience in the Biden administration provided a platform for her candidacy as she sought to build a coalition of supporters.

The race to succeed the current governor is expected to be closely watched by national political observers and party leaders. Control of state governorships remains a significant focus for both Democrats and Republicans, as governors shape policy on issues ranging from education and healthcare to economic development and environmental regulation.

As Haaland moves forward to the general election, she will face the task of expanding her primary coalition to include independent voters and persuadable Republicans in the general electorate. The outcome in New Mexico will contribute to the broader narrative about Democratic performance in 2024 and the direction of state politics in the Southwest.

Haaland's victory in the Democratic primary represents an important achievement in her political career and opens the possibility of a historic governorship if she wins in November.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced Saturday that it has launched an investigation into election fraud in California's elections. The probe comes as vote counting continues in several key races across the state.

The announcement follows unsubstantiated claims by President Trump and other conservatives about irregularities in California's vote-counting process. Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy also criticized the state's vote-counting procedures, saying California voters were losing faith in the process as results continue to come in from Tuesday's primary elections.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters should not receive pardons
cards.teaser: The former vice president said those who assaulted police or vandalized the Capitol should not be pardoned by President Trump.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Friday that those who attacked police, damaged government property, or worked to disrupt the 2020 election certification should not be pardoned by President Trump. He made the remarks during an interview on HBO's Real Time.

Pence's position directly contradicts Trump's approach to handling January 6 convictions. His comments mark his sharpest rebuke yet of potential pardons for those involved in the Capitol attack.

cards.headline: White House AI policy adviser to step down at end of month
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a senior White House adviser on artificial intelligence, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this month.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a senior White House adviser on artificial intelligence, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this month. Krishnan, a tech investor who became a key figure in the Trump administration's AI efforts, helped develop strategic plans for the president's artificial intelligence goals.

Krishnan's departure marks a significant shift in the White House's AI policy team as the administration works to maintain U.S. competitiveness in artificial intelligence development. The senior policy adviser played a central role in coordinating the government's approach to AI regulation and innovation.

The Trump administration has made artificial intelligence a policy priority, viewing the technology as critical to national security and economic growth. Krishnan's work included shaping how the federal government approaches AI development, deployment, and oversight across various agencies and sectors.

No replacement has been announced for the position. The timing of Krishnan's departure comes as Congress debates legislation related to AI safety and regulation, and as the administration faces questions about how to balance innovation with safeguards. The White House has not provided details about Krishnan's plans after leaving the administration.

The departure adds to a series of staffing changes in the Trump administration as it approaches the midterm elections. AI policy has become increasingly important to the federal government as the technology advances rapidly and raises questions about privacy, security, and economic disruption.

cards.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press as approval ratings hit new lows
cards.teaser: The president faces an interview Sunday following a turbulent week and growing tensions with Senate Republicans.
cards.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday following a week of declining approval ratings and escalating tensions with Senate Republicans. The appearance comes as the president faces mounting political pressure ahead of the midterm elections.

Trump's relationship with congressional Republicans has grown strained, potentially affecting his ability to advance his legislative agenda. The interview takes place during a turbulent period marked by public disputes between the president and members of his own party.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are ahead in early results from the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton leads the Republican field while Xavier Becerra has advanced to the general election among Democrats in California's governor primary. The race determines the top two candidates to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

Becerra's advancement marks a stunning turnaround for the former Biden cabinet official, whose campaign was struggling with near 3% polling support in late March. If elected in November, he would become California's first Latino governor since 1875. The primary results have been delayed, prompting the U.S. Justice Department to send a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles.

cards.headline: McCarthy criticizes California vote count after Trump fraud claim
cards.teaser: The former House Speaker echoed criticism of the state's vote-counting process as results from the primary continue to arrive.
cards.body:
Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy criticized California's vote-counting process on Friday, echoing claims made by President Trump and other conservatives. McCarthy told hosts on WABC 770AM that California voters were losing faith in the process as results continued trickling in from Tuesday's elections.

California's slow ballot count has drawn criticism from political observers and prompted Trump to accuse Democrats of trying to steal elections for governor and Los Angeles mayor. The Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles. Election experts say California's deliberate pace reflects built-in verification systems designed to prevent fraud and ensure every vote counts accurately.
